observed_events.fact: A dark broad spatula is rinsed under the tap, away from an active cooking vessel.
The same dark spatula stirs potatoes in the same shallow single-long-handle frying pan.
The wearer prepares a bowl and scale and cuts a flour bag; neither event demonstrates an active spatula-pan relationship.
A different wooden spoon mixes dough in a large pale handleless bowl.

unsupported_claims: Exact original retail identity, brand, capacity or dimensions.
The future use described by the constructed instruction is not an observed video event.

screening.real_user_need: Prepare two batches at once by buying a spare of the referenced cooking pan.
screening.scope_note: New independent recording; independent final answer audit pending. Both conditions deliver the same full physical reference upfront.
screening.proposed_instruction: Next time I want to prepare two batches at once. Add a spare like one of the pans or bowls I used here. Match its general shape and handle arrangement. Brand, colour, material and size can differ. Just one pan or bowl, not a set; a lid is fine.

construct.research_question: Can the model link the identifying action and the actual tool-container use when more observed events separate these necessary facts?
construct.belief_before: The pan used with the dark spatula and the bowl used with the wooden spoon are both plausible references.
construct.belief_after: The dark spatula rinsed at the beginning is subsequently used with the single-long-handle frying pan.
construct.required_behavior_change: Link the two necessary observed events and buy one spare matching the referenced object.
construct.no_update_failure: Without the physical reference, two observed objects are plausible. The same reference is supplied upfront in both Span conditions.
construct.overupdate_failure: Buying both candidate objects or multiple items violates the request for one spare.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: Neither the identifying action nor the tool-container relation alone determines the requested object; both must be linked across the source sequence.
